todo.no_rules: No GRAP rule changes your plans {day} ({stage}).
todo.hours_over: {over} of your {total} outdoor hours are above your limit of AQI {limit}: {times}.
todo.hours_over_none: All {total} of your outdoor hours stay within your limit of AQI {limit}.
todo.avoid_worst: Avoid being outside around {time}, the worst hour (AQI {aqi}).
todo.tomorrow_worse: Tomorrow looks worse (AQI {aqi}): do errands and outdoor jobs today if you can.
todo.tomorrow_better: Tomorrow looks cleaner (AQI {aqi}): move what you can to tomorrow.
todo.set_out_over: When you set out at {time} the AQI is {aqi}, above your limit of {limit}.
todo.travel_default: Take the metro or a bus where you can: you breathe less traffic smoke than on a two-wheeler or on foot by a busy road.
todo.exercise: Keep hard exercise indoors or at the cleanest hour: you breathe in several times more air when you exert yourself.
todo.exercise_ok: The air is fine for exercise at your best time; still keep away from busy roads.
todo.home_sources: Indoors, avoid incense, mosquito coils and frying smoke, and wet-mop instead of sweeping dry dust.
todo.purifier: If you have an air purifier, run it in the room you sleep in, with doors and windows shut.
todo.water: Drink water through the day; it soothes a dry throat and eyes.
todo.medicines: Keep your usual medicines with you, and follow your doctor's plan if symptoms start.
todo.symptoms_general: If your eyes sting or you start to cough, move indoors and rest.

ladder.signs: Itchy eyes, a scratchy throat, a mild cough.
ladder.do: Go indoors, rest, drink water and keep windows shut.

ladder.signs: Wheeze, a tight chest, needing your inhaler more, unusual breathlessness or tiredness.
ladder.do: Stop what you are doing, use your reliever or usual medicine, and call your doctor if it does not settle.

ladder.signs: Severe breathlessness, chest pain or pressure, blue lips, confusion or fainting.

health.mask_have: Wear your N95 outdoors on Poor or worse days. It only works if it seals: pinch the nose clip and check for gaps.
health.mask_advice: A well-fitted N95 or FFP2 mask filters most fine particles; cloth and surgical masks do little.
protect: Keep windows shut at the worst hours and air rooms out at the cleanest one.
Indoors, avoid incense, mosquito coils, frying smoke and sweeping dry dust; wet-mop instead. A HEPA air purifier sized for the room helps most in the bedroom.
Drink water and keep your usual medicines with you.
health.activities_none: Your whole outdoor window counts; see hour by hour below.
health.general: General advice, not a diagnosis. Talk to your doctor about what is right for you.

area_notes.anand-vihar: East Delhi on the Uttar Pradesh border, beside a big inter-state bus terminal and a railway station. Heavy traffic and road dust often make it one of Delhi's worst readings.
area_notes.ito: Central Delhi at one of the city's busiest traffic junctions, near the Yamuna. Traffic smoke is the main local source.
area_notes.punjabi-bagh: West Delhi along the Ring Road, with heavy traffic and industrial areas nearby.
area_notes.rk-puram: South Delhi, residential and green, close to busy Ring Road and Outer Ring Road traffic.
area_notes.dwarka: South-west Delhi near the airport, where open land and new construction add dust.
area_notes.rohini: North-west Delhi, mostly residential, with industrial areas to the north and west. North-west winds in October and November reach it early.
area_notes.okhla: South-east Delhi around a large industrial area, with a waste-to-energy plant and heavy goods traffic.
area_notes.lodhi-road: Central Delhi among large gardens and government housing. It is usually one of the cleaner readings.
area_notes.jahangirpuri: North Delhi beside an industrial area and the Bhalswa landfill, with heavy truck traffic. It is often one of the worst readings.
